text:
Maya (PM): Quick sync — we need a decision on long-term platform routing & isolation. Customers keep asking for per-tenant geo pinning + SLA tiers. Running out of time for Q3 roadmap. Thoughts?

Ajay (Eng): +1. Options: 1) Strong tenant-affinity (dedicated slices per-customer), 2) Soft-affinity with fast failover to pooled capacity, 3) Region-aware single pool with data-tagging. Each has perf/cost/ops implications.

Kevin - Infra: Breakdown: (1) predictable tail latency but ~3x cost for low-util tenants; (2) lower cost, more complex fallback logic and debugging; (3) best for privacy/regulatory if we implement strict residency routing, but higher networking complexity. Need concrete numbers to compare.

Sam R.: Customer ask from FinCo: must guarantee >95% requests served in EU region and no cross-region data movement. That basically forces option 1 or a region-isolated pool with hard residency. They will not accept soft fallbacks.

Devon (SRE): Launch gating we should require: SLA verification harness, automated region outage simulation, and tail latency targets at 95th/99th under 2x normal QPS. Also need per-tenant audit logs for routing decisions.

Ajay (Eng): Also consider model-variant fallback policies. When dedicated slices are exhausted, fallback to a quantized model in a hosted pool with explicit latency caps. Example policy snippet: 

```yaml
policy:
  tenant_affinity: hard
  allowed_fallbacks:
    - model: redwood-quant-8bit
      max_latency_ms: 300
  regions: [eu-west-1]
  audit: enabled
```

Maya (PM): Nice. Can we get cost delta estimates for each option and a customer impact matrix? Need these to prioritize features for roadmap.

Kevin - Infra: I'll run a capacity/cost simulation. Need assumptions: tenant QPS distribution (p50/p90/p99), percent of tenants requiring strict residency, and expected growth. If someone can share those I'll plug them in.

Sam R.: I'll collate customer asks and identify 3 pilot customers (one fintech, one healthcare, one enterprise SaaS) for early testing and sign-off. Will include residency constraints per customer.

Devon (SRE): Observability requirements: expose per-tenant routing path, model variant selected, and an immutable audit trail for data residency audits. Prometheus metrics + traces + a lightweight per-tenant timeline in the console.

Ajay (Eng): Implementation sketch: Phase 0 — routing policy DSL + policy evaluation service; Phase 1 — soft affinity + deterministic fallback rules + canary rollout; Phase 2 — hard affinity + reservation pool + billing adjustments; Phase 3 — regional evacuation, cross-region repair, and migration tooling.

Maya (PM): OK let's target Phase 0 & 1 for H1 next year. Acceptance criteria for Phase 1: DSL spec reviewed, e2e tests (including simulated region fail), canary plan defined, and cost-beta for 10 pilot tenants with telemetry.

Kevin - Infra: Action: I'll deliver simulation numbers by Thu. Ajay — can you draft the DSL spec by Wed? Devon — can you draft SLO tests and the outage-sim job? Sam — share the pilot customer list by EOD Monday.

Ajay (Eng): On it.

DevOps Bot: Deployment note — spec-draft branch created and scheduled for review tomorrow 10:00am. :robot_face:

Maya (PM): Thanks team. We'll sync Friday 11am to sign off and assign owners to the Phase 1 tickets.
